issues.legal_issue: A lease-like transfer of mineral rights by a lessee falls within the statutory meaning of a mining lease even when it is described as a sublease.
material_facts: The company held a mining lease and transferred rights over part of the leased area to another person for a term and consideration.
The transfer was for mining purposes and created a right to enjoy immovable property.
issues.conclusion: A mining sublease is included in the definition of a mining lease and is subject to the Act and the Rules.
issues.legal_principle: Section 3(d) of the Mines and Minerals (Regulation and Development) Act, 1948, broadly defines a mining lease by its purpose and does not require the lessor to be the proprietor. Under section 105 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, a lease is a transfer of a right to enjoy immovable property; the transferor’s own title does not alter the nature of the transaction. Section 108(j) of the Transfer of Property Act recognizes a lessee’s ability to transfer an interest by sublease. The Court also relied on the regulatory purposes reflected in sections 5 and 6 of the 1948 Act and referred to Camberwell and South London Building Society v. Holloway (1879) 13 Ch. D. 754, 759, for the principle that a lease remains a lease when granted by someone who is themselves a leaseholder.

predicates.sublease_transaction: A person holding a lease transfers an interest in the leased property to another person, with the transferor being a lessee rather than the owner.
predicates.mineral_extraction_purpose: The transferred interest is granted for searching for, extracting, working, or otherwise dealing with minerals.
predicates.lease_like_transfer: The transfer grants a right to enjoy immovable property for a term or in perpetuity in return for consideration.

issues.definition: When a lessee makes a lease-like transfer of property for mineral purposes, that transfer counts as a mining lease.

issues.legal_issue: Rules governing mining leases apply to a mining sublease made after those rules take effect, even if the lessee’s own lease predates them.
material_facts: The company’s original mining lease was granted before the Act and the Rules came into force in the relevant area.
The company granted the sublease after the Act and the Rules had come into force there.
The sublease was a mining lease within the statutory definition, and the challenged prosecution concerned the later grant rather than a change to the terms of the original lease.
issues.conclusion: Rules made under sections 5 and 6 apply to a mining sublease granted after the Act and the Rules come into force, notwithstanding that the underlying lease predates them.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 5 and 6 of the Mines and Minerals (Regulation and Development) Act, 1948, authorize rules governing mining leases. Section 7 concerns modifying or altering the terms of mining leases granted before the Act commenced; it does not prevent rules under sections 5 and 6 from applying to a distinct mining sublease made after the Act and Rules have come into force. Because a sublease is itself a mining lease under section 3(d), applying the rules to the later sublease does not modify the earlier lease.

rule.if: mining_sublease_transaction and underlying_lease_preexisting and mining_rules_were_in_force and sublease_made_after_rules_took_effect

predicates.mining_sublease_transaction: A lessee transfers an interest in leased property to another person for mineral-related purposes.
predicates.underlying_lease_preexisting: The transferor’s own lease was granted before the relevant mining rules took effect.
predicates.mining_rules_were_in_force: Rules regulating mining leases had taken effect in the area covered by the transferred interest.
predicates.sublease_made_after_rules_took_effect: The lessee granted the sublease after those rules had taken effect in that area.

issues.definition: A mining sublease made after the mining rules take effect is governed by those rules even when the underlying lease was granted earlier.
